minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved a new recreation director's hiring grade and step, but delayed the compensation plan to a Wednesday meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee approved amended minutes of March 6 and the HR Director's recommended grade and step for the new recreation director. Most of the meeting was a discussion of the consultant's compensation study: members said it isn't ready, questioned the comparison data and the consultant's timeline, and debated whether to aim for the finance committee date or push to November. A tentative Wednesday meeting was set.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none offered at the start.
An employee (Pauline) asked whether the proposal used the new scale or the current projection, and urged the committee to address under-market pay that employees have waited over a year on.
An employee asked why the consultant's grid uses two percent steps when the town historically used three percent, and said she'd send questions to the consultant.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to accept the HR Director's recommended grade and step for the new recreation director; Joanna was not connected.
Most of the meeting went to the consultant's compensation study, which members said is not ready; no decision on the plan was reached.
Members agreed to keep pressing to finish the compensation plan rather than defer it to November.
Members will send questions on the plan to the HR Director to forward to the consultant, including why the grid's step increases are smaller than the town's past ones.
A committee meeting was tentatively set for Wednesday, pending Joanna's availability, to give the consultant time to answer.

why_it_matters: The compensation plan sets town employee pay ranges and feeds the FY24 payroll line, so a delay leaves employees who say they are paid under market waiting and leaves the cost of the plan open as the budget is built.
Whether pay changes are retroactive if the grid is pushed back a year was raised and left unresolved, and the draft cost leaves out beach staff and call fire staff.

The finance committee date versus a November target for the compensation plan, which members had not settled.
